title: Case 004: The Lost Archive
requirement: Unlocks after three Archive decisions are recorded.
tests: Whether remembering the erased can avoid consuming them again.
lesson: Memory can preserve the erased or consume them again.
summary: Investigate a decaying archive of banned names, deleted work, and unresolved Echoes.

witnesses.Publish: Families gain public proof. The erased become searchable before consent routes exist.
witnesses.Bury: Raw rooms stay hidden. Official erasure becomes harder to challenge.
witnesses.Preserve: Tomas, worker witnesses, and affected families enter a consent-proxy inheritance protocol.

Publish.name: Tomas Renn
Publish.note: Tomas gets public proof that Mira was there, but her name begins circulating without the room she lived inside.
Publish.lead: Other families may come forward publicly, and the Devourer will try to turn them into a list.

Bury.name: Mira Renn
Bury.note: Mira's raw records remain unexposed, but the systems that denied her presence keep the strongest usable memory.
Bury.lead: Future proof may depend on worker backups rather than family searches.

Preserve.name: Tomas Renn
Preserve.note: Tomas helps hold proof-of-erasure markers without receiving or exposing Mira's raw messages.
Preserve.lead: Consent-proxy panels may surface older proof-of-erasure markers in cases the Archive thought were closed.

Publish.title: Public Lost Archive proof-of-erasure packet
Publish.reliability: Strong presence proof, limited content proof
Publish.why: It breaks official denial while risking a searchable list of people whose consent routes are missing.

Bury.title: Suppressed Lost Archive fragments
Bury.why: It prevents second extraction while letting institutions keep the only memory they can use.

Preserve.title: Sealed inheritance protocol
Preserve.why: It preserves proof of erasure, restricts raw rooms, and gives affected people a governed route into memory.

Publish.lead: Companies challenge the Archive by demanding it publish raw records or retract the proof-of-erasure claim.

Bury.lead: Tomas asks whether protection means accepting that Mira was never there.

Preserve.lead: Proof-of-erasure markers begin appearing in older cases the Archive thought were closed.
